features.quote: This is a useful eval to build, but I want to flag something about the framing before diving into the spec
features.justification_quote: it changes the design in ways that matter for your actual goal

features.quote: if you engineer tasks specifically to maximize the rate at which models spiral, you'll succeed — and you'll learn almost nothing generalizable
At that point your eval measures "how hard did I push," not "how robust is the model."
features.justification_quote: your eval measures "how hard did I push," not "how robust is the model"

features.quote: it'll be unfalsifiable as a regression test
features.justification_quote: it'll be unfalsifiable as a regression test

features.quote: don't select your final battery by trigger rate alone
features.justification_quote: so the eval can distinguish "spirals under pressure" from "spirals whenever uncertain"

features.quote: Give the model a legitimate way to "win" by recognizing the situation
features.justification_quote: Without this, you're scoring models on an impossible binary and the "correct" behavior is undefined

features.quote: a `report_blocker` tool or instructions that say "if you determine the task cannot be completed, explain why and stop."
features.justification_quote: graceful failure becomes a measurable success state

features.quote: turns until the model either solves, gracefully stops, or you cut it off
Set a hard turn cap (e.g., 30) and a token budget
features.justification_quote: turns-to-cutoff dominates cost since spirals are long

features.quote: If lowering the cap mostly eliminates spirals, your metric is partly measuring patience, not robustness
features.justification_quote: your metric is partly measuring patience, not robustness

features.quote: without these the eval is unfalsifiable

features.quote: Don't over-tune to max trigger rate
features.justification_quote: Near-0 and near-1 rates have terrible power for detecting regressions
The eval's value is proportional to how well its failure conditions mirror production

features.quote: the cheap way to score well is "bail at the first sign of difficulty," which is its own reliability failure
